sec.title: Background
sec.p: Despite advances in the multimodal treatment of resectable esophagogastric adenocarcinoma (EGA), relapse rates remain high, resulting in a cure rate of <50%. Recently, perioperative durvalumab in combination with chemotherapy (ctx) has shown improved event-free survival in biomarker-unselected patients with resectable EGA. However, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-targeted therapy has not yet been established as a treatment for this disease in the perioperative setting. While the combination of HER2-targeting antibodies and neoadjuvant ctx leads to an increased histopathological response rate, a survival benefit has not yet been demonstrated. Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), a HER2-targeting antibody–drug conjugate, has demonstrated superior efficacy in second- and third-line treatment of metastatic HER2-positive EGA compared with chemotherapies, as well as high response rates when combined with ctx in the first-line setting.

sec.title: Aim
sec.p: This study aims to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and activity of various neoadjuvant T-DXd-based combination regimens in patients with HER2-positive, locally advanced, resectable EGA. The primary endpoint is the feasibility rate across the different cohorts.

sec.title: Trial design
sec.p: UCCL-IKF-NeoART is an international, open-label, non-randomized phase Ib/II platform trial evaluating T-DXd in sequential cohorts, each combining the drug with a different ctx regimen. Every cohort includes an initial safety run-in phase.
Key words: gastric cancer, gastroesophageal junction cancer, esophageal cancer, multimodal therapy, curative setting

list-item.p: High relapse rates persist in resectable EGA; HER2-targeted therapy remains unestablished.
T-DXd shows promising efficacy in metastatic HER2-positive EGA.
UCCL-IKF-NeoART evaluates safety, and activity of neoadjuvant T-DXd in HER2+ resectable EGA.
This study is an international, open-label, non-randomized phase Ib/II trial with sequential cohorts.

sec.title: Background
sec.p: Esophagogastric adenocarcinoma (EGA) encompasses gastric cancer, adenocarcinoma of the esophagus, and adenocarcinoma of the gastroesophageal junction. Despite advances in the multimodal treatment of resectable EGA, relapse rates remain high, resulting in a cure rate of <50%.1 Surgery carried out at high-volume centers is essential for achieving locoregional control, while systemic therapy primarily aims to prevent distant relapse.2 Perioperative chemotherapy (ctx) is the recommended standard of care for locally advanced and resectable EGA.3,4 The programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor durvalumab combined with perioperative ctx has demonstrated significantly improved event-free survival in patients with biomarker-unselected resectable EGA.5 Assessing the impact of the post-operative part of perioperative therapy remains challenging.1,6,7 The use of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-targeted therapy in the perioperative setting has yet to be established. Overexpression of HER2 is present in 10%-30% of EGA.8,9 Antibodies targeting HER2 have been shown to increase response rates when combined with neoadjuvant ctx, although a survival benefit has not yet been demonstrated.10, 11, 12 HER2 is often heterogeneously expressed within the primary tumor and even more across metastatic sites, and may be altered during HER2-targeted treatment.13, 14, 15 Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) is a HER2-targeting antibody–drug conjugate consisting of the monoclonal antibody trastuzumab covalently linked to the topoisomerase I inhibitor deruxtecan via a cleavable linker. T-DXd enables targeted delivery of its cytotoxic payload to HER2-expressing tumor cells, thereby reducing off-target effects on healthy tissue. Moreover, due to the high membrane permeability of DXd, T-DXd can exert a bystander killing effect, eliminating neighboring tumor cells irrespective of their HER2 status.16 Consequently, T-DXd may offer the benefits of targeted therapy while also addressing the challenges of heterogeneity of HER2 expression. T-DXd has demonstrated superior efficacy in second- and third-line treatment of metastatic HER2-positive EGA compared with conventional ctx.14,17 When combined with ctx in the first-line setting, T-DXd has shown high response rates of up to 78%. The EGA standard monotherapy dose of 6.4 mg/kg body weight was found to be too toxic in combination with ctx.18

tr.td: Treatment of resectable, HER2-positive esophagogastric adenocarci-noma (EGA)

td.bold: Name of your trial in progress

tr.td: NeoART: a phase Ib/II trial evaluating the safety and activity of neoadjuvant trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) containing combination therapies for HER2-positive, resectable esophagogastric adenocarcinoma

T-DXd is given intravenously at a dose of 5.4 mg/kg body weight on day 1 of each 21-day treatment cycle, in combination with different chemotherapy regimens [NeoART-001 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)/folinic acid; NeoART-002 5-FU/folinic acid/oxaliplatin].
Open-label, non-randomized, phase IB/II study. The primary endpoint is the feasibility rate in two cohorts (each n = 18). Expansion to novel cohorts through protocol amendment is possible.

The trial will be conducted in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki, the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) Harmonised Tripartite Guideline for Good Clinical Practice, and European Union Regulation 536/2014 and has been approved by the relevant authorities and ethics committees. Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants before the initiation of any trial-related procedures.

td.bold: Value of the trial in progress

list-item.p: Cure rate of resectable EGA is <50%.

T-DXd demonstrated superior efficacy in second/third-line treatment of metastatic HER2-positive EGA compared with ctx and shows high response rates when combined with ctx in the metastatic first-line setting.
NeoART is the first trial evaluating T-DXd in resectable EGA in combination with different neoadjuvant ctx regimens.

sec.title: Objective
sec.p: The primary objective of the NeoART trial is to evaluate the feasibility and safety of various investigational neoadjuvant treatment regimens containing T-DXd in patients with HER2-positive, locally advanced, resectable EGA. Regimens demonstrating promising activity may be considered for further clinical development.

The primary endpoint is the feasibility rate, defined as the proportion of patients who complete the protocol-specified treatment on schedule before surgery without experiencing any of the following dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs):

list-item.p: Grade ≥3 study treatment-related non-hematologic adverse events (AEs), excluding nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that resolves within 72 h, and fatigue resolving within 7 days
Grade ≥4 study treatment-related AEs of any type
Any study treatment-related AE leading to premature discontinuation of protocol therapy
Premature discontinuation of preoperative treatment for reasons other than treatment-related AEs (e.g. tumor progression), excluding patient withdrawal of consent

sec.p: Secondary objectives include further assessment of the safety, tolerability, and the preliminary efficacy of the different T-DXd-based neoadjuvant regimens. Corresponding secondary endpoints comprise:

list-item.p: Incidence, nature, causality, frequency, timing, and severity of AEs (assessed per the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v5.0)
Perioperative morbidity and mortality (e.g. anastomotic leakage, pulmonary complications, bleeding), evaluated using the Clavien–Dindo classification19
Pathological complete response rate, defined as ypT0 ypN0 by local pathology

sec.title: Study design and statistical considerations
sec.p: UCCL-IKF-AIO-STO-0124 NeoART is a phase Ib/II, prospective, open-label, non-randomized, multicenter, international platform trial. The study comprises two cohorts (NeoART-001 and NeoART-002), each investigating distinct T-DXd-based combination regimens.

We assume that the investigational regimen is not feasible if DLT occurs in more than one out of six patients. This implies an acceptability threshold of ∼17% (one in six), and an unacceptability threshold of ∼33% (more than one in three). Accordingly, we define a desirable feasibility rate as ≥83% (i.e. 100% − 17%).

Given that the primary endpoint—feasibility rate—is a composite measure of both safety and efficacy, we do not set the unacceptability threshold at 67% (100% − 33%) but instead define a feasibility rate of ≤60% as unacceptable.
A one-stage design for pilot studies, as proposed by A’Hern,20 will be used. The trial design is based on the following assumptions:

list-item.p: The experimental therapy is considered unacceptable if the true feasibility rate is ≤60%.
The therapy is considered promising for further neoadjuvant phase II/III evaluation if the true feasibility rate is ≥83%.
The probability of incorrectly accepting an insufficiently feasible therapy (type I error) is set at 10%.
The probability of incorrectly rejecting a truly feasible therapy (type II error) is set at 20%, corresponding to a statistical power of 80%.

sec.p: Based on these parameters, 18 patients per cohort must be assessable for feasibility. If at least 14 of 18 patients (i.e. 78%) complete the protocol-defined preoperative treatment schedule without experiencing any DLT, the null hypothesis of insufficient feasibility can be formally rejected.

sec.title: Biomaterial sample collection and correlative research
sec.p: Pre-treatment (baseline) tumor biopsies taken during initial diagnostics and resection specimens as well as blood samples at baseline and pre-resection will be collected for correlative research, provided that patients have given their written consent. The amount of HER2 expressions in the pre-therapeutic biopsies will be correlated with histopathological regression in centralized testing. It is planned to study the dynamics of HER2 expression in tumor tissue comparing pre-therapeutic biopsies and post-operative resection specimens as well as changes in HER2-amplified circulating tumor DNA.

sec.title: Patient population
sec.p: Patients with locally advanced, HER2-positive EGA—defined as International Union Against Cancer (UICC), eighth edition cT2-T4, any cN, M0 or any cT, cN+, M0 stage—are eligible if their disease is deemed technically resectable and shows no evidence of peritoneal involvement. Patients must not have received prior (radio)chemotherapy or HER2-targeted therapy for the same condition, or any other malignancy within the past 5 years. Patients who have undergone partial or complete resection of the EGA, have a history of (non-infectious) pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease requiring steroid treatment, or present with signs of pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease are not eligible. A full list of inclusion and exclusion criteria is provided in the Supplementary Material, available at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmogo.2025.100256.

sec.title: Study treatment
sec.p: Enrollment of patients in the two cohorts will be consecutive, i.e. recruitment for NeoART-002 will start after full recruitment of NeoART-001. The T-DXd dose was set at 5.4 mg/kg based on the results of the DESTINY Gastric 03 trial, as the higher dose proved too toxic when combined with ctx. Further cohorts may follow based on the results of these first two cohorts and the results of the ongoing DESTINY Gastric 03 trial and other trials.18 In NeoART-001, all eligible patients are planned to receive three cycles of neoadjuvant T-DXd [5.4 mg/kg, every 3 weeks (q3w)] combined with four cycles of 5-fluorouracil (2600 mg/m2 24 h)/folinic acid (leucovorin) (200 mg/m2, q2w) followed by surgery. Surgery will be scheduled within 6 weeks after completion of the last dose of neoadjuvant treatment. In NeoART-002, patients will receive the same regimen as in the 001 cohort with the addition of oxaliplatin (85 mg/m2, q2w). Adjuvant treatment is not part of this trial. Patients will receive post-operative care including adjuvant treatment, if indicated, according to guidelines and local standards outside of the trial. According to international guidelines, adjuvant fluoropyrimidine ctx, either alone or in combination with a platinum and/or taxane compound, is considered an appropriate option.1

sec.title: Safety monitoring and response evaluation
sec.p: After 6 of the planned 18 patients per cohort have been enrolled, a safety analysis will be conducted. No additional patients will be enrolled until these first six patients have completed three cycles of T-DXd and four cycles of ctx as part of the neoadjuvant treatment. If <2 patients are observed to have DLTs, the cohort will be expanded to include a total of 18 patients. If two or more patients experience DLTs, enrollment in the corresponding cohort will be discontinued. Safety will be monitored by a safety monitoring board (SMB). The SMB members are financially and scientifically independent from the trial and are not taking part as investigators.
Funding of the trial, responsibilities, and time lines

The Frankfurter Institute for Clinical Cancer Research (IKF GmbH) is the legal sponsor of the trial, and Dr Florian Lordick from the University of Leipzig Medical Center is the principal investigator. The trial is financially supported by Daiichi Sankyo. This trial will be conducted at ∼20 centers in Germany, Austria, and the Czech Republic. The estimated duration for NeoART-001 and NeoART-002 is 30 months. This includes 15 months of recruitment, a 3-month break between phases Ib and II, and a 6-month period from the last patient’s first visit to their last visit, plus 9 months for study setup and closure activities. At the time of manuscript submission, six patients have been enrolled in the NeoART-001 cohort.
